text:
Alex C: FYI customer reported sudden p95/p99 spikes on hosted-api after we flipped the int8 quant profile last week. They started seeing 2-3x tail latency for long-context requests.
Maria S: Which customer? any correlation with model/seq len?
Alex C: AcmeFin (ticket #4521). Model: redwood-34b-qlora, typical seq_len ~ 4096, but some requests go to 8192. Spikes start around 1h after profile rollout.
Samir P: I saw a related alert on infra — autoscaler thrashing + lots of fallback to FP16 kernels in logs. Might be calibration/overflow on int8 path.
Jordan (support): AcmeFin sent a sample repro payload. I ran it against our canary endpoint and reproduced p99 ~ 1.8s (baseline 0.6s). Log snippet attached.
Alex C: paste logs please. we need stack traces / kernel switch events.
Jordan (support): here: ```
2024-11-05T18:22:15Z INFO  request_id=xx kd=kv_cache_hit=false seq=8192 profile=int8
2024-11-05T18:22:15Z WARN  fallback_kernel=fp16 reason=overflow_detected kernel_switch_ms=120
2024-11-05T18:22:15Z INFO  attention_opt=block_sparse attempt=1
2024-11-05T18:22:16Z WARN  latency_ms=1786
```
Samir P: that kernel_switch_ms=120 is huge and explains p99. It suggests the runtime is trying int8, detecting numeric instability, then reinitializing fp16 path mid-request. That reinit cost + slower fp16 run = tail spike.
Maria S: Why would overflow be detected only after 1h? calibration might be data-dependent. Did we use a narrow calibration dataset for int8 profile?
Alex C: The profile was auto-calibrated on a small sample (1000 tokens) from open-web corpus. Not representative of AcmeFin's finance data.
Jordan (support): Customer says their traffic has lots of long numeric tables and rare token distributions. That could trigger quantization saturation.
Samir P: Two quick mitigations: 1) disable int8 for that deployment (roll back to fp16) 2) add a quick guard to avoid mid-request kernel switches by failing fast to fp16 at request start (incurs consistent cost but avoids 120ms penalty).
Maria S: Can we patch the runtime to check calibration headroom before serving and choose fp16 at route-level? Minimal change: consult quant_profile.headroom metric at request admission.
Alex C: Agreed. For immediate customer relief, Jordan — can you switch their serving profile to fp16 and confirm latency?
Jordan (support): On it. Pushing config: ```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/admin/deployments/DEPL-ACMEFIN/config -d '{"quant_profile":"fp16"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>'
```
Jordan (support): Update: config applied. Re-running sample -> p99 now 0.62s. Customer confirming. :relieved:
Alex C: Great. Next steps for engineering: reproduce locally and add regression test. Samir — can you create a perf test that simulates AcmeFin payload distribution and verify quant profiles?
Samir P: Yes. I'll write a benchmark harness to run across int8/fp8/fp16 at seq_len 4096/8192 with skewed numeric tokens. Will also instrument time spent in kernel switch and init.
Maria S: Also add a canary gating rule: after any quant profile rollout, run a 1h synthetic workload that samples top customers' distributions in prod and fail rollout if tail latency increases >20% vs baseline.
Alex C: Good. Ops question: do we have telemetry for "quant_profile.kernel_switch_count" per route? If not, add it.
Samir P: We currently log switch events but not aggregated. I'll add a metric counter and an alert when switch_count > 5 per minute per route.
Jordan (support): Customer asked whether fp8 would be safer than int8 for them. Quick answer?
Maria S: fp8 has better dynamic range but is still early on our runtime. We observed fewer switch events vs int8 in internal tests but a small set of samples showed occasional quality regressions. Not ready for broad auto-rollout. For now recommend fp16 for critical, high-tail workloads.
Alex C: Need an internal postmortem doc: include timeline, root cause (calibration mismatch + runtime mid-request kernel reinit), mitigations applied (rollback to fp16 + canary gating + metric), and follow-ups (better calibration, pre-flight headroom check, kernel_switch counter). Jordan, can you file the ticket and notify AcmeFin?
Jordan (support): Filed DOC-7897 (customer comms + support runbook). Pinged AcmeFin with explanation and ETA for a more durable fix (2 weeks).
Samir P: I'm going to prototype a pre-calibration step: run a quick per-route dynamic range analyzer that estimates if int8 headroom < threshold, then mark route as "do-not-int8". If it looks good, we still do int8 but with a static fallback path (no mid-request reinit).
Maria S: Add unit tests for sequences with repeated large exponent tokens (e.g., long numeric arrays) — we missed that in initial calibration.
Alex C: Also attach a guide for SEs: how to quickly rollback quant_profile, how to run the local repro tool, and how to read kernel switch logs. Jordan, please add to support KB.
Jordan (support): Will add KB entry under support/quantization_retries.md. Drafting now.
infra-bot: Alert: canary rollout of quant-profile-int8 completed on 2024-11-05 17:15 UTC for 45% of hosts.
Alex C: Note for release: disable auto-int8 rollouts until we have improved calibration and gating. Everyone ok?
Maria S: thumbs up from me.
Samir P: +1. I'll target the kernel_switch metric and the pre-flight analyzer in next sprint.
Jordan (support): Customer confirmed service stable after rollback. Closing ticket when we publish KB and planned fix.
Alex C: Thanks all. We'll follow up in eng-runtime weekly with a short demo of the analyzer.
Maria S: Also consider adding a toggle to prefer consistent latency over peak cost when choosing quantization per-customer. That'll make product folks happy.
Samir P: noted. I'll include cost/latency tradeoff flags in the PR.
Jordan (support): Closing note: customer asked for a one-time credit for the degraded performance window. Finance ok with 10% credit. I'll handle it. :+1:
